title: Key usage attribution & audit-proxy runbook (v0.1 draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:

This runbook is a working draft for implementing a lightweight audit-proxy layer and key-usage attribution pipeline for Private deployments (VPC / on-prem). Goal: provide deterministic, forensically useful audit records tying encryption operations (KMS/HSM) back to request context, without leaking plaintext or increasing customer blast radius.

Context / motivators (why do this now):
- Customers ask for better auditability of key operations for compliance (SOC2 + regulated verticals).
- Current KMS integrations record only key IDs and high-level outcome; we lack request-scoped attribution (which route, which tenant, which container/node).
- On-prem and VPC deployments have diverse network topologies; we need a deployable pattern that works with HSM-attested nodes and cloud-managed KMS fallbacks.

Non-goals:
- Do not attempt to centralize plaintext logs. We must avoid storing PII / secrets in audit trails.
- Not addressing application-level trace capture beyond minimal identifiers (route id, request id).

High-level design sketch (informal):
- Introduce an audit-proxy service that sits alongside KMS adapter in the control plane for Private deployments. Proxy responsibilities:
  - Receive encrypted/opaque key operation metadata from node agents (kms-sidecar or sealed-kms-adapter).
  - Enrich with local attestation metadata (node ID, workload ID, enclave/TPM attestation blob reference), but only store hashes/refs in logs.
  - Normalize and forward compact audit events to: local audit log (append-only file with WORM mode on air-gapped installs) and optional remote Aggregator (for Dedicated/backplane).
  - Provide idempotent event ingestion and sequence numbers for replays reconstruction.

Event shape (minimal required fields):
- timestamp (RFC3339)
- event_id (UUID)
- op_type (encrypt|decrypt|wrap|unwrap|rotate)
- key_id (customer-key-id or wrapped-key-id)
- actor_hash (sha256 of ephemeral actor identifier; reversible only by customer with local mapping)
- request_id (redwood request id or tenant-provided request id)
- node_hash (sha256 of node identity attestation; non-reversible)
- attestation_ref (opaque short id pointing to attestation blob stored separately, or a short signed certificate fingerprint)
- outcome (success|failure|retry)
- reason (optional short code)
- tf_module_version (string)

Key points: store only hashes for node and actor for cross-run correlation without exposing raw hostnames. attestation blobs kept in a segregated store with stricter access control and separate retention policy.

Terraform module notes (rough, provider-agnostic):
- Module: modules/kms_audit_proxy
  - resources:
    - deployment of audit-proxy (k8s deployment or systemd unit for airgap)
    - ConfigMap / file mount for local WORM log path + rotation policy
    - ServiceAccount with minimal RBAC to read attestation artifacts, and to call KMS adapter endpoints
    - Optional ms-aggregator endpoint config (for non-airgapped installs)
  - Inputs:
    - audit_log_path (string)
    - worm_enable (bool)
    - max_event_size_bytes (int)
    - attestation_store_uri (string)
  - Outputs:
    - audit_proxy_endpoint
    - audit_proxy_version
  - Upgrade notes:
    - Make explicit migration path for existing logs: include an adapter that computes event sequence numbers from old logs, and emits a migration event pointing to an arc of legacy logs. Keep legacy logs read-only after migration.

Migration / upgrade plan (high level steps):
1) Canary: deploy audit-proxy in canary namespace on dedicated nodes in staging. Configure nodes to emit a duplicate event stream (existing KMS logs + audit-proxy).
2) Verify: run correlation checks on sample tenant traffic; confirm event shape, no plaintext, attestation refs resolvable.
3) WORM test: for air-gapped installs use attested USB fallback to verify append-only retention.
4) Rollout: staged rollout to non-critical racks, monitor ingest rates and disk usage.
5) Cutover: switch node agents to primary-forward to audit-proxy and keep old pipeline read-only for 30d.
6) Post-mortem and retention trimming: ensure attestation blobs older than 180 days are rotated out as per customer policy.

Operational considerations and failure modes:
- Network partitions: audit-proxy must buffer in local persistent queue (fs-backed) and retry with exponential backoff. Design for OOM prevention: bounded queue + drop policy with local alert on drop.
- HSM downtime: if HSM rejects op, emit a failure event with reason code and avoid retrying keys without manual review.
- Replay attacks: sequence numbers + event HMAC using proxy-local signing key (kept in HSM if available). Remote aggregator verifies signature.
- Scaling: event rate correlates to token consumption; expect spikes during batch jobs. Recommend default disk sizing: 1GB per 100k events retention window.

Security & privacy controls (must-have list):
- All audit events signed with proxy key (rotate quarterly).
- Attestation blobs stored separately with KMS-protected encryption keys. Access logged and audited.
- Hash-only identifiers in main audit trail. Only customer-owned tooling can map hashed actor -> real identity (we provide optional per-customer mapping tool that runs in their control plane).
- Tamper-evidence: when writing local logs, compute and append chained-hash footprint (chain-of-trust) and periodically publish checkpoint hashes to the aggregator or to the customer’s transparency ledger.

Testing checklist (quick):
- unit: event schema validation, hash-only fields, signing/verification
- integration: simulated node agent emits events, attestation ref stored + retrievable, aggregator verifies HMAC
- chaos: disk full, network drop, HSM reject, proxy restart with unflushed queue
- privacy: confirm no secret or plaintext appears in any audit event or enrichments

Sample operational queries (for aggregator):
- Count decrypt failures per key last 24h
- Top nodes (hashed) invoking wrap operations last week
- Requests with attestation failures and the associated reason codes

Open questions / TODOs (triage needed):
- Should actor_hash be reversible by Redwood Ops under certain legal processes? Currently plan is NO; only customer-side mapping tooling. Need legal review.
- How do we surface sequence numbers to customers without leaking infrastructure layout? Propose per-tenant sequence namespace.
- Terraform: standardize naming convention across onprem and VPC modules (naming collision risk).
- Integrations: work with eng-observability to add ingestion metrics and dashboards (slo: 99.9% events within 3s of op).

Quick wins / next steps (owner: Marina):
- Draft a minimal PoC: audit-proxy container (go) that accepts json events and appends WORM file + signs events. (2 wks)
- Create TF module scaffold and add to infra repo for review. (1 wk)
- Book joint review with SRE + security + solutions engineering. (this sprint)

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- consider Otel trace linkage but only via hashed trace id to avoid correlation leakage
- keep attestation blobs externally verifiable (customer can check signatures with their root)
- tie this into existing secrets-telemetry pipeline but with stricter access controls and retention

References and links: see linked_artifacts above. Also: internal note on WORM fs options, prior KMS fallbacks RFC (CONFLUENCE-SEC-966).

End of draft. This doc is intentionally informal — lots of TODOs and open questions. Feedback welcome; please add comments inline or push to the linked GitHub PR for code sketches.
